clue.text: A pretty rad comic playing the blues?

indicators.note: playing suggests performing or toying with something, so these words are rearranged rather than read as they stand

parts.note: all fifteen letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A fairly edgy comedian performs some blues numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing the blues' paints music, but in US politics blue is the colour of the Democrats, so the blues are the DEMOCRATIC PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: On American electoral maps Democratic states are coloured blue, so its supporters and the party itself are called the blues.

clue.text: Four people getting together to describe Ike's monogram?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: two couples going out together
second meaning: a whimsical description of initials that start with a repeated letter

explanation.walkthrough: Ike was President Dwight D. Eisenhower, whose monogram DDE starts with a doubled D; the question mark flags the playful reading of the answer as a description of those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A double date is an outing where two couples go together, so four people in all.

clue.text: Sad one is more disturbed about vessel

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the vessel goes inside
disturbed means thrown out of order, so the word's letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: A grieving person grows more upset over an urn.
explanation.walkthrough: The urn suits the funeral picture, but it is just a container in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A mourner is a person grieving for someone who has died, so a sad one.

clue.text: Young crowds of trees

parts.note: Cy Young was the celebrated baseball pitcher, so Young suggests his first name
to crowd and to press are both to push close together

explanation.surface: Groves of saplings packed close together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young' looks like an adjective for young trees; it is the surname of the baseball pitcher Cy Young, and leads to his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cypresses are coniferous evergreens, a familiar kind of tree.

clue.text: Match a resident of Athens incompletely

indicators.note: incomplete means unfinished, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: taken as written
Athens is the capital of Greece

explanation.surface: Pairing someone up with an Athenian, only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that agree correspond, so to agree is to match or tally.

clue.text: Author Murdoch and that man — indeed, they are sometimes smiling

parts.note: Iris Murdoch was the Anglo-Irish novelist
the pronoun for a man
indeed and yes both affirm

explanation.surface: A novelist and a man, apparently cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the old song 'When Irish Eyes Are Smiling'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title 'When Irish Eyes Are Smiling' makes these the eyes famously described as smiling at times.

clue.text: Bit of paint on impressionist's sheet

indicators.note: a bit is a small part, here just the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of paint
an aper is a mimic, someone who apes others like an impressionist

explanation.surface: A dab of paint on a Monet's canvas sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' suggests Monet; here it is a mimic. In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet is a single leaf of paper, so the words are used interchangeably.

clue.text: 25 found in dilapidated minaret

indicators.note: a dilapidated building has fallen into disrepair, so its letters are in a broken order

parts.note: all seven letters of the tower are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something discovered inside a crumbling mosque tower.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 25-down, GARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing, which is what garb means too.

clue.text: Origins of yarn: "Everest's terrifying iceman!"

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so the opening letters are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: The source of a mountaineer's tall tale about a monster in the Himalayan snows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' is a tall story, which fits the legend of the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti, or abominable snowman, is the legendary ape-like creature said to roam the Himalayan snows.

clue.text: Wrongful ruler from America bombed Peru before onset of revolution

parts.note: US is the standard abbreviation for the United States

indicators.note: something bombed is blown apart, so the word that follows is scattered into a new order

parts.note: the country's name supplies four letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the onset of anything is its beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of revolution

explanation.surface: A tyrant from the US devastates Peru, an act that sparks the start of a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just puts the scrambled country ahead of the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurper seizes a throne or power without the right to it, so is an illegitimate sovereign.

clue.text: Stamp — one in perfect condition — involves hype

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to involve is to take something in, so the condition word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: mint condition means as new, never used
PR, public relations, is the business of hype

explanation.surface: A stamp collector describes a perfect-condition stamp being talked up with hype.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes and philatelic flavour make 'Stamp' look like a postage stamp; here it means a mark pressed into something.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprint is a mark left by pressing, the same thing as a stamp made on a surface.

clue.text: Thrust 19 épées on the left

parts.note: the cross-reference points to the answer at 19, organ, and a lung is one example of an organ

indicators.note: the leftmost part of a written word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of épées

explanation.surface: A fencer's thrust, with the swords held on the left side.
explanation.walkthrough: The 19 refers to 19-across, ORGAN, and a LUNG is defined by example; fencing terms make 'Thrust' look like part of the scene, and it is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is the fencer's forward thrust with the weapon, so the two words name the same attacking move.

clue.text: Rethink 3+10 with a computer communication system

indicators.note: to rethink is to reorganise one's ideas, so the letters are reorganised into another order

parts.note: the numeral written out as a word
the numeral written out as a word

explanation.surface: Someone redoing a sum with a computer network.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like cross-references to 3 and 10 in the grid; here they are simply the words three and ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the standard wired networking technology linking computers in a local network.

clue.text: Russian opera reportedly runs with blood online?

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the phrase's sound is what counts

parts.note: a publication that runs gory material prints gore

explanation.surface: A Russian opera is said to stream with blood on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' is publishing, not flowing: a site that runs gory content prints gore, which said aloud is the title of Borodin's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Igor is Alexander Borodin's Russian opera, famous for its Polovtsian Dances.

clue.text: What you might play in a pub: a backward violin

definitions.text: What you might play in a pub

indicators.note: going backward means reading from the last letter to the first

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius, the famous make of violin

explanation.surface: Pub entertainment: a fiddle played badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'backward violin' suggests a bad fiddler in the corner of the pub; the violin is the short name of the Stradivarius.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is the classic British pub game of throwing small arrows at a board on the wall.

clue.text: Someone who handles money for the Rev. Spooner, a clergyman, in springtime

indicators.note: William Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words are exchanged

parts.note: a minister in the fifth month of the year, with the opening sounds then swapped

explanation.surface: A treasurer talks about Spooner, a cleric seen in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring gives MAY and a clergyman is a PASTOR; swapping their opening sounds gives PAY MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A paymaster is the official responsible for paying out wages and funds.

clue.text: North of European country, pornography becomes hollow, burning desire?

indicators.note: hollowing a word scoops out its middle, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of pornography
Romania is a country in south-eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Censorship in the north of a European country leaves its porn trade empty.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'North of' puts one piece above the other. The definition is literal: a desire for burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is a compulsion to start fires, so it is quite literally a desire for burning.

clue.text: Oh, a crappy alternative for Judith, Susanna, etc.

indicators.note: an alternative version is a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: all nine letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a poor substitute for some biblical heroines.
explanation.definitionFit: Judith and Susanna are books of the Apocrypha, the texts outside the Hebrew Bible canon.

clue.text: Flowing tears concealing certain values

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so one piece goes within the other
flowing implies running loose and changing shape, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: five letters to be rearranged
certain and sure are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone weeping freely while hiding their real convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Values' is a verb here, to prize something, not a noun about principles.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to hold it dear, which is what it means to value it.

clue.text: Chained savage anteater

indicators.note: to savage is to maul and tear apart, so the word's letters are torn into a new order

parts.note: all seven letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fierce anteater kept on a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is the spiny anteater of Australia and New Guinea, an egg-laying mammal.

clue.text: J.P. is missing front of medical instrument

indicators.note: missing the front means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: J. P. Morgan was the American financier and banker

explanation.surface: A justice of the peace has lost the front part of a surgical tool.
explanation.walkthrough: J.P. looks like a justice of the peace; it is the banker J. P. Morgan. The definition is playful: an organ is a musical instrument and also a body part of medical interest.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is both a keyboard instrument and a body part doctors treat, so a 'medical instrument' is a punning description.

clue.text: Lose sight of sailor with the Swedish Nightingale

parts.note: gob is American slang for a sailor
Jenny Lind, the 19th-century soprano, was known as the Swedish Nightingale

explanation.surface: A sailor loses track of the famous Swedish singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose sight of' reads as one phrase, but 'of' only links: the definition is losing one's eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: To go blind is to lose the sense of sight altogether.

clue.text: Ill-made hat mauls part of the brain

indicators.note: something badly made is put together wrongly, so these letters come in a jumbled order

parts.note: all eight letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shoddy hat crushes the wearer's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The thalamus is a structure deep in the brain that relays sensory signals to the cortex.

clue.text: Disabled Israeli's letter

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a letter of the Hebrew alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a letter sent by an Israeli; it is a letter of the alphabet used in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamed is the twelfth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, and also the past participle of lame, meaning crippled.

clue.text: Wickedness, from the time of Christ until now

parts.note: sin is moral wickedness
CE, Common Era, is the dating era running from the traditional birth of Christ to the present

explanation.surface: Evil has been with us throughout the Christian era.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the secular replacement for AD in dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Since is a preposition meaning starting from a past point, as in 'since Monday', i.e. counted from that time onward.

clue.text: Polish and French for the capital of Russia

parts.note: to polish something is to rub it
le is French for the word the, the next word of the clue

explanation.surface: A question about Polish and French names for Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is a verb, not the nationality, and 'capital' is money, not a city like Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruble (also spelt rouble) is the Russian currency, and capital can mean money.

clue.text: Boast about clothing

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: to boast is to brag

explanation.surface: Showing off about one's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for dress or attire, especially of a distinctive kind.

clue.text: Swallowing piece of dirt, bemoan upset stomach

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one letter goes within the other word
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: a piece is only a small part, here just the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the first letter of dirt

explanation.surface: Someone who has eaten some dirt complains of a stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset stomach' reads as an ailment, but 'upset' works on the letters before it and 'stomach' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdomen is the belly, the part of the body that holds the stomach and is loosely called the stomach.

clue.text: Terrible GNP pain is out

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: the economic abbreviation for gross national product plus pain give the seven letters

explanation.surface: An economist laments that the country's output is suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like economic news but means asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone napping is asleep, and 'out' is an informal way of saying unconscious or asleep.

clue.text: Drink a generic product around school with hesitation

indicators.note: around means placed on either side, so the product wraps the school

parts.note: Brand X is the stock name for an unnamed generic product in advertising
Yale is the Ivy League university in Connecticut
with and and both mean together with
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A student hesitates over a cheap own-label drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brandy Alexander is a cocktail of brandy, crème de cacao and cream.
